title: Cross-site scripting (XSS)
prompt_md: # Coding problem, 5.1.b: Fix the Reflected Comment **Skill:** Mitigate Risk · **Maps to:** 5.1.A, 5.1.B · **Language:** Python 3 (pytest) ## The situation `render_comment` builds the HTML that shows a visitor's comment on a page. It works for ordinary text, but it drops the username and comment **straight into the HTML** by string concatenation. That is reflected cross-site scripting (XSS): whatever the user typed is parsed by the next visitor's browser as markup, so `` in a comment becomes a live script running in that visitor's session. The starter is the vulnerable version. A comment of `` comes back out as a real `
starter_py:

USERNAME: COMMENT

Fix it with context-aware OUTPUT ENCODING: HTML-encode each user value (html.escape(value, quote=True)) before placing it into the template, so the browser can never parse user input as markup. Do not strip or blocklist input; keep the structural
/ tags as real HTML. """ return '
' + username + ": " + comment + "
"

interface_md:
# Interface, 5.1.b-encoded-comment Any implementation that satisfies this interface can be swapped in (reference, student, or composite) and must pass the tests unchanged. ## Entry point ```python def render_comment(username: str, comment: str) -> str ``` ## Input - `username`: the commenter's display name (untrusted input). - `comment`: the comment body (untrusted input). ## Output A single HTML string, the comment card: ```
USERNAME: COMMENT
``` where `USERNAME` and `COMMENT` are the HTML-encoded forms of the two inputs. ## Encoding rules - User values are HTML-encoded with `html.escape(value, quote=True)` semantics: `&` → `&`, `<` → `<`, `>` → `>`, `"` → `"`, `'` → `'`. - The structural markup the function itself emits (`
`, ``, ``, `
`) is real HTML and is **not** encoded. - No detection, stripping, or blocklisting of input. Encoding alone is the defense. ## Guarantees / rules - Pure function, deterministic, no I/O, no network. Standard library only (`html`). ## Acceptance Your code passes when every test below shows a checkmark (some are hidden until you run them). user values are encoded rather than concatenated raw.
